checks: A sufficiently large finite signed tilt isolates either endpoint fiber without changing its own continuous cut. Its depth at x is p_e(1−|x|)/2, maximized uniquely at zero. Both nonvertical orientations and pure-base cuts respect that lower bound.

At middle mark zero, normal reflection reduces the nonvertical cuts to X+az≥0. Endpoint fractions are F(a) and 1−F(a), while the own fraction is one half. The finite slopes a=±1 attain the minimum endpoint contribution. Through-mark pure-base caps are no better.

Depth superlevel sets are convex by the midpoint test on every closed containing halfspace. Reflection of X fixes the weighted law and implies that zero maximizes within the middle fiber. Subtracting the middle maximum from the larger endpoint maximum gives exactly (R+3|D|−2)/4.

The positive Gaussian weights are unequal at the two endpoints almost surely at each fixed positive finite time, since A_t has a Gaussian mixture density. Every term in the maximum is strictly below 1/2 then. The a.s. posterior limit is a point mass and the same continuous formula tends to 1/2, so the expectation cannot be monotone in either direction.

Exact rational replay at t=2 log 2 and a=log 8 gives weights (1,16,64)/81 and maxima 1/162, 1/9, 32/81. Their strict ranking and full-support mixture density give the open positive-probability event. At either limiting endpoint atom the corresponding maximum is strictly greater than the other two, so eventually the unique winner is its center.
